descriptors.concept_name: Objective of Additional Communication in Auditor Report
descriptors.definition: The auditor draws users' attention to matters fundamental to understanding the financial statements or relevant to understanding the audit, responsibilities, or report through clear additional communication. This is performed after forming an opinion on the financial statements when judged necessary.
inclusion: Matters fundamental to understanding financial statements
Matters relevant to understanding audit responsibilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from audit opinion modification which alters the overall reporting conclusion
Distinguished from key audit matters governed under specific reporting standards

descriptors.concept_name: When to give Emphasis of Matter Paragraphs in the Auditor's Report?
descriptors.definition: An auditor includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph to highlight a properly presented or disclosed matter that is fundamental to the users' understanding of the financial statements. This requires that the matter does not trigger a modified opinion under SA 705 and is not already determined to be a key audit matter under SA 701.
inclusion: Frameworks prescribed by law that would otherwise be unacceptable
Special purpose framework financial statements
Subsequent events discovered after report date requiring a new report
exclusion: Matters requiring an adverse or qualified opinion
Matters classified as key audit matters
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Other Matter paragraphs which refer to items not presented inside the financial statements

descriptors.concept_name: Inclusion of an Emphasis of Matter Paragraph in the Auditor’s Report
descriptors.definition: When including an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, the auditor must place it in a separate section with a specific heading and clearly reference the disclosures inside the financial statements. The paragraph must explicitly indicate that the auditor's opinion remains unmodified regarding the emphasized matter.
inclusion: Exceptional litigation uncertainty
Significant subsequent events
Early application of a new accounting standard
Major catastrophes impacting financial position
exclusion: References to information outside the financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from reporting requirements for Other Matter paragraphs which cover items not presented in financial statements

descriptors.concept_name: Distinction Between Notes on Accounts and Qualifications
descriptors.definition: Notes on accounts represent management viewpoints and disclosures, whereas audit qualifications express the auditor's formal disagreement or modification regarding accounting treatment. An Emphasis of Matter is not a substitute for an opinion modification when the underlying matter warrants a qualification.
inclusion: Management explanations via financial statement notes
Auditor disagreements expressed through report qualifications
Quantified opinions expressed using except for phrasing
exclusion: Using Emphasis of Matter as a substitute for opinion modification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Emphasis of Matter, which applies to properly presented items rather than uncorrected misstatements or scope limitations requiring qualification

descriptors.concept_name: Distinction Between Audit Report and Certificate
descriptors.definition: An audit report communicates an expression of professional opinion on financial statements, whereas a certificate involves verifying specific factual matters or observations. Under statutory provisions, certain actions require factual certification rather than an opinion-based report.
inclusion: Opinion-based reports under statutory sections
Fact verification statements such as asset inspections
exclusion: Issuing reports when factual confirmation is strictly mandated
Issuing certificates for general financial statement opinions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the level of assurance; reports convey professional opinions, while certificates confirm concrete factual findings

descriptors.concept_name: Communication to Management and Those Charged with Governance
descriptors.definition: The auditor must communicate necessary audit matters to those charged with governance regardless of entity structure or size. Special considerations apply when governance and management roles overlap or when dealing with subgroup structures like audit committees.
inclusion: Communications with designated governance subgroups
Communications where governance and management roles coincide
exclusion: Redundant communications to individuals acting solely in management capacities without oversight roles
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine operational communications with general company staff

descriptors.concept_name: When All of Those Charged with Governance are Involved in Managing the Entity
descriptors.definition: When all governance individuals are also involved in managing the entity, communicating required matters to those persons fulfills the governance communication obligation. The auditor must still ensure that this communication adequately informs everyone who would otherwise receive it in a governance capacity.
inclusion: Single owner-managed entities
Combined management and governance roles
exclusion: Entities with segregated boards of directors and separate executive management teams
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard governance structures requiring separate formal reporting streams away from executive managers

descriptors.definition: The auditor must communicate auditor responsibilities, planned scope, timing, and significant findings derived from the audit to those charged with governance. This includes discussing accounting practices, significant difficulties, and matters affecting the form of the audit report.
inclusion: Auditor's role in forming financial statement opinions
Overview of planned audit scope and significant risks
Significant qualitative aspects of accounting practices
exclusion: Relieving management of their core financial statement preparation duties
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from internal working papers not meant for governance review

descriptors.concept_name: Planned Scope and Timing of the Audit
descriptors.definition: The auditor provides those charged with governance with an overview of the planned scope and timing of the audit. This communication specifically encompasses details regarding the significant risks identified by the auditor.
inclusion: Overview of audit planning parameters
Identification and communication of significant audit risks
exclusion: Detailed internal audit testing steps or proprietary audit programs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from post-audit findings because it occurs during the planning phase prior to substantive testing completion

descriptors.definition: The auditor communicates significant audit findings, including qualitative aspects of accounting practices, accounting policy choices, and significant difficulties encountered during the audit. Additional items include written representations requested and circumstances affecting the auditor report format.
inclusion: Auditor views on accounting estimates and disclosures
Deviations from most appropriate accounting practices
Significant matters discussed with management
exclusion: Trivial operational matters lacking governance relevance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial scope planning communications by focusing on actual findings and issues uncovered during execution

descriptors.concept_name: Reporting Requirements in Case of Comparative Information
descriptors.definition: Auditors handle comparative information using either corresponding figures or comparative financial statements under specific reporting frameworks. The auditor must gather sufficient evidence ensuring comparative figures comply with framework requirements and remain consistent with prior periods.
inclusion: Ensuring agreement with prior period disclosures
Evaluating policy consistency or proper disclosure of changes
Obtaining written representations for prior period items
exclusion: Treating corresponding figures as separate full-period audit opinions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by whether the opinion covers only the current period versus covering each presented period individually

descriptors.definition: The auditor performs procedures to verify comparative information, ensuring policy consistency and evaluating potential misstatements against prior accounts. Specific reporting rules dictate when prior period figures alter current opinions or require Other Matter paragraphs.
inclusion: Procedures when prior period reports contained other than unqualified opinions
Procedures when unaddressed prior material misstatements exist
Disclosing substantive reasons for changed prior opinions
exclusion: Referring to corresponding figures in current opinions unless specific prior exceptions occur
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard current-period testing by focusing specifically on historical comparative balances and opening positions
